title: Documenting and Handing Over Automation knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Documenting and Handing Over Automation?
options: Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
A useful handover includes workflow purpose, trigger conditions, required variables/secrets by name only, action ownership, runbooks, dashboards, and rollback instructions.
questions.answer_key: A useful handover includes workflow purpose, trigger conditions, required variables/secrets by name only, action ownership, runbooks, dashboards, and rollback instructions.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of documenting and handing over automation: A useful handover includes workflow purpose, trigger conditions, required variables/secrets by name only, action ownership, runbooks, dashboards, and rollback instructions. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to documenting and handing over automation?
options: Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: A useful handover includes workflow purpose, trigger conditions, required variables/secrets by name only, action ownership, runbooks, dashboards, and rollback instructions. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
